entries.title: GDP, (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 3rd Quarter 2026
entries.detail: Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 4.3 percent in the third quarter of 2026 (July, August, and September), according to the second estimate released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). In the second quarter, real GDP increased 2.2 percent. The contributors to the increase in real GDP in the third quarter were increases in investment, consumer spending, and government spending that were partly offset by a decrease in exports. Imports, which are a subtraction in the calculation of GDP, increased.

entries.title: Personal Income and Outlays, October 2026
entries.detail: Personal income increased $201.8 billion (0.7 percent at a monthly rate) in October, according to estimates released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). Disposable personal income (DPI)–personal income less personal current taxes–increased $200.5 billion (0.8 percent), and personal consumption expenditures (PCE) increased $63.8 billion (0.3 percent). Personal outlays–the sum of PCE, personal interest payments, and personal current transfer payments–increased $69.3 billion in October. Personal saving was $1.00 trillion, and the personal saving rate–personal saving as a percentage of DPI–was 4.1 percent.
